cohort: 487 pregnant women at the University of New Mexico between March 1, 2020 and March 24, 2021
finding: Mothers with COVID-19 during pregnancy had a significantly higher rate of cesarean deliveries (33% vs. 20%) and delivered at an earlier gestational age (37.6 vs. 38.5 weeks) compared to uninfected mothers.
mod_finding: Mothers who tested positive for COVID-19 during pregnancy were significantly more likely to deliver via cesarean section compared to COVID-negative mothers (33% vs. 20%).
gest_age: Infants born to mothers with COVID-19: 37.6 weeks, Infants born to mothers without COVID-19: 38.5 weeks
